reforms.description: The US is taking policy actions to improve quality secondary education, based on the recommendations of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) 2010 report Prepare and Inspire, including supporting state-led standards for secondary education and making investments toward preparing 100,000 more STEM-qualified teachers over the next decade.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving STEM education is expected to enhance the quality of the workforce, thereby supporting innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The policy actions have been publicly announced but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative to prepare more STEM-qualified teachers represents a significant but narrower reform in education policy.
reforms.source_quote: The US is taking policy actions to improve quality secondary education, based on the recommendations of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) 2010 report Prepare and Inspire.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform focuses on improving quality secondary education and preparing 100,000 more STEM-qualified teachers, which aligns with human capital for R&D.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Administration has proposed increases in Federal support of R&D, most recently in the 2015 Budget proposal of USD 135.4 billion, a nominal increase of 1.2% over 2014, along with a supplementary proposal of USD 5.3 billion for R&D related to 'Opportunity, Growth, and Security'.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased federal R&D funding is expected to enhance innovation and productivity, contributing positively to economic growth.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The budget proposal has been enacted and funding is being allocated as planned.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The proposed increase in federal R&D funding represents a significant policy change aimed at boosting research and development efforts.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The Administration has proposed increases in Federal support of R&D, most recently in the 2015 Budget proposal of USD 135.4 billion.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: While it mentions increases in Federal support of R&D, the description lacks a clear government adoption signal and is based on a past budget proposal.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Administration has proposed increases in Federal support of R&D, most recently in the 2015 Budget proposal of USD 135.4 billion, alongside the creation of an Energy Security Trust Fund to support innovation in energy-saving technology and low carbon technology. Additionally, the America COMPETES Act established the Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy, which funds energy technology projects to promote innovation in energy efficiency and low carbon technology.
all_reforms_including_excluded.package_name: Federal R&D and Energy Innovation Support
all_reforms_including_excluded.component_name: R&D Funding and Energy Trust Fund
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased funding for R&D and energy innovation is expected to enhance productivity and technological advancement.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The proposals are part of the 2015 Budget and other announcements.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The reforms represent significant increases in federal R&D funding and the establishment of a dedicated trust fund for energy innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The Administration has proposed increases in Federal support of R&D, most recently in the 2015 Budget proposal of USD 135.4 billion, a nominal increase of 1.2% over 2014.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The proposal includes funding for energy technology projects, but the primary focus is on capital deployment through the Energy Security Trust Fund, not direct R&D funding.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Under the Administration’s Preschool for All initiative, States would need to meet quality standards to receive federal funds, including requiring preschool teachers to have a bachelor degree and ongoing professional development, as well as requiring higher preschool staff salaries.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving preschool education quality is expected to enhance early childhood education outcomes and support future innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The initiative is part of the Administration's proposals for early childhood education.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant policy change aimed at improving early childhood education standards.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Under the Administration’s Preschool for All initiative, States would need to meet quality standards to receive federal funds, including requiring preschool teachers to have a bachelor degree and ongoing professional development.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform pertains to preschool education quality standards and teacher qualifications, which does not directly relate to R&D or human capital for R&D.
